name: Question 20
problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}-48y-10x+59=0.$
worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}-48y-10x+59 & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}-48y-5{x}^{2}-10x+59 & =0 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-12y]-5[{x}^{2}+2x]+59 & =0 \\ 4[(y-6)^{2}-36]-5[(x+1)^{2}-1]+59 & =0 \\ 4(y-6)^{2}-144-5(x+1)^{2}+5+59 & =0 \\ 4(y-6)^{2}-5(x+1)^{2} & =144-5-59 \\ 4(y-6)^{2}-5(x+1)^{2} & =80 \\ \frac{(y-6)^{2}}{20}-\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16}=1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(-1,6),\,a=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5},\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
y-6=\pm \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}(x+1).
$$

Question 20
?

Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola 4y2−5x2−48y−10x+59=0.

a
y+1=±255(x−6)
b
y−6=±52(x+1)
c
y+1=±52(x−6)
d
y−6=±455(x+1)
e
y−6=±255(x+1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the x and y terms and complete the squares, as follows:

4y2−5x2−48y−10x+59=04y2−48y−5x2−10x+59=04[y2−12y]−5[x2+2x]+59=04[(y−6)2−36]−5[(x+1)2−1]+59=04(y−6)2−144−5(x+1)2+5+59=04(y−6)2−5(x+1)2=144−5−594(y−6)2−5(x+1)2=80(y−6)220−(x+1)216=1

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

(y−k)2a2−(x−h)2b2=1

are given by

y−k=±ab(x−h).

In our case, we have

(h,k)=(−1,6),a=20=25,b=16=4.

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are y−6=±52(x+1).
